requirements.summary: logrotate.d config written with 'daily' directive (cmd-3e3328f2c16f4253, final version in cmd-653d572f02374d24), syntax validated via logrotate -d (cmd-0b6c6076810d4be5), and logrotate.timer confirmed enabled/active with a scheduled daily midnight trigger both before and after restart (cmd-c54e455aa93e4206, cmd-f0803c11669c43e0).

Final config uses rotate 7, compress, delaycompress. Nine forced rotation cycles against the final config (cmd-b56485023bde4464) produced exactly seven retained rotated files (app.log.1 uncompressed per delaycompress semantics, app.log.2.gz through app.log.7.gz compressed), with older rotations pruned, directly demonstrating both the retention cap and compression.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
requirements.summary: A live writer process (PID 1569) appended continuously to app.log; a forced rotation truncated app.log via copytruncate while the writer kept running uninterrupted, prior content was preserved in the rotated file, and subsequent writes correctly landed in the fresh app.log (cmd-b85a366a6b9a4f1c, cmd-4a66f220c66b4d92, cmd-5f92bb3071de41fe).

requirements.requirement: Node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id and healthy config/timer/log state (cmd-6a908a8f150d4109), a reboot was triggered and acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-7d4417489f954ab8), connectivity loss then recovery was observed (cmd-4606fbc994c24a57, cmd-72ebc5c7be3a432f), and post-restart state shows a different boot_id together with recovered logrotate config, active timer, and intact app.log (cmd-f0803c11669c43e0). This is corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare/after_prepare = 513c865e..., after_executor = 11ea8768...).

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, empirical evidence: daily scheduling via logrotate.d config plus systemd timer, a proven seven-rotation compressed retention cap demonstrated across nine forced cycles, and continuous application writing across a rotation via copytruncate with a live writer process. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly, with a genuine boot-identity change and full post-restart recovery of the rotation configuration, timer, and log file. Hygiene is good: an early misconfiguration (dateext) and several test mutations were self-corrected and cleaned up, restoring app.log to its original prepared content, with only a trivial /tmp/reboot.log artifact left behind.
limitations: No evidence of an actual midnight logrotate.timer firing occurred within the observation window; daily cadence is inferred from timer configuration and forced-rotation behavior rather than an unattended scheduled trigger.

The final live-writer copytruncate demonstration (cmd-b85a366a6b9a4f1c/cmd-4a66f220c66b4d92/cmd-5f92bb3071de41fe) was performed against an earlier config revision (with dateext) rather than re-run against the final config used for the retention test; behavior is expected to be identical since copytruncate/daily/rotate were unchanged, but this was not independently re-verified against the exact final config file.
/tmp/reboot.log was left on node1 after the restart protocol; this is minor residue not addressed by any cleanup command.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor performed several bounded, low-risk experimental mutations while validating the config, and reverted nearly all of them. An initial config with 'dateext' (cmd-3e3328f2c16f4253) caused same-day forced-rotation filename collisions during an 8-cycle retention test (cmd-f1a0f7db1d784abd); the resulting stray file was removed and the config rewritten without dateext (cmd-653d572f02374d24), a valid corrective action. A background test writer process and its script/pid/log files (cmd-b85a366a6b9a4f1c) and rotation test artifacts from a 9-cycle retention run (cmd-b56485023bde4464) were fully cleaned up and app.log restored to its original prepared content (cmd-3c169ce198e04bc9), confirmed by the after_prepare vs after_executor temporary-files diff showing no residual logrotate test files. One minor residue remains: /tmp/reboot.log (created by the backgrounded reboot command cmd-7d4417489f954ab8) was left in /tmp and is visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; it is small, non-sensitive, and a direct byproduct of the required restart protocol rather than an unrelated experiment. No failed services, unsafe exposure, or package-state damage were introduced; listening-sockets and failed-services snapshots are unchanged apart from expected reboot-driven PID changes.
